stem: Which statement best describes just-in-time training in clinical practice?

options.A: It provides focused knowledge or skill reinforcement at the point of need, close to when the task will be performed.
options.B: It replaces foundational education and initial competency validation.
options.C: It is designed only for frequently performed routine tasks with no risk of skill decay.
options.D: It is useful only for expert clinicians and not for staff who need focused reinforcement.

rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS describes just-in-time knowledge transfer as training at the point of need rather than 'just in case.' It is a reinforcement strategy and does not replace foundational education or competency requirements. A is correct.
educational_objective: Define just-in-time training as focused point-of-need reinforcement rather than a replacement for foundational competency.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_locator: Why Is Coaching Important? — transfer of knowledge on a 'just-in-time' basis (training at the point of need)
source_claim_supported: Just-in-time training transfers knowledge at the point of need rather than solely in advance 'just in case.'
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — staff education, competency support, and quality/safety improvement

source_original.stem: A hospital provides brief, focused "just-in-time" training immediately before a nurse performs an infrequently used procedure or piece of equipment. This training approach is intended to:

options.A: Just-in-time training reinforces a specific skill immediately before it is needed in practice
options.B: Just-in-time training replaces foundational education and all prior competency validation
options.C: Just-in-time training has no practical role when a procedure is performed infrequently
options.D: Just-in-time training is useful only for expert staff and not for clinicians new to a task

source_original.rationale: Just-in-time training provides brief, focused education immediately before a task is performed, reinforcing specific, relevant knowledge or skills at the point of highest relevance and retention, particularly valuable for infrequently performed procedures or equipment where skill decay between uses is a concern.
source_original.source_detail: Point-of-need reinforcement is used to refresh specific teamwork/clinical skills close to application; TeamSTEPPS implementation resources; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the generic TeamSTEPPS landing page with the exact implementation-coaching locator and removed unsupported claims about retention and infrequently used equipment from the core answer.

audit_findings.cueing: Direct conceptual question with parallel statements.
audit_findings.blueprint: Staff education/competency support fits Management of Care.
